method: L10r2 attempt 1, src/tools/repair.ts at 43,594 B: prompt_tokens 10,549 + completion_tokens 5,960 = 16,509 against the model's REAL loaded contextLength of 16,384, confirmed by `lms ps`. finish_reason stop, category elided, probe applied 0 of 1. The corrective retry: 10,549 + 5,947 = 16,496, also over, also stop, truncated
note: THE VOID CONDITION IS NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN INFERRED. contextExhausted against the REAL 16,384 returns true and catches this response; against the 32,768 the artifact recorded it returns false and calls the only content-losing response of the run a fit. 125 tokens is the whole margin -- the failure does not need a dramatic overshoot, which is exactly why the declared window has to be verified rather than trusted

method: Same case, both attempts. The diagnostic appends the whole 5,960-token bad response plus a corrective message before attempt 2, so attempt 2's message list is roughly 6,000 tokens larger. The server reported prompt_tokens 10,549 for BOTH, and attempt 2 still generated 5,947 completion tokens
note: EVIDENCE ON THE contextOverflowPolicy OPEN POINT, FROM TOKEN ACCOUNTING RATHER THAN FROM READING THE SETTING. Under stopAtLimit a prompt that alone exceeds the 16,384-token window could not have produced ~6,000 tokens of answer; under truncateMiddle or rollingWindow LM Studio prunes the prompt and keeps generating, which fits both the identical reported count and the completion. NOT PROOF -- the server could also be reporting a cached-prefix figure -- but it is the first observation that discriminates between the policies at all, and it points the same way as the closed-block-with-90-lines-missing that opened the question

method: First run whose declared window was verified against the loaded one: LOCAL_CODER_CONTEXT_TOKENS=32768 with `lms ps` reporting contextLength 32768 for qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-instruct-dwq-v2, checked by the command that launched it. 26 requests, 26 scored, 0 errored, 0 refused: complete 26, elided 0, truncated 0, probe applied in every file of every response. Largest admitted request 20,870 actual tokens against a 29,491 usable budget, clearing B16's 70% non-void bar of 20,644
note: B16 DOES NOT FALL, AND DOES NOT YET HOLD. Its fall condition is >10% of admitted requests losing content: 0 of 26. Its hold condition is 0 over at least 20 admitted requests across at least TWO non-void runs, and this is one -- mac-19 is void for declaring a window the model did not have. One more non-void run settles it. Recorded this way deliberately: 0 of 26 reads like a pass, and reading it as one would be the slippage this file exists to prevent

method: The same request at two real windows. src/tools/repair.ts, 43,594 B, prompt 10,549 tokens both times. At a real 16,384 window (run 2026-08-04-mac-19-32k) the model emitted 5,960 completion tokens and elided; at a real 32,768 it emitted 10,321 and returned complete with the probe applied. Room left after the prompt at 16,384 was ~5,835 against the 10,321 the file actually needs
note: THE ELISION WAS ARITHMETIC, NOT MODEL QUALITY, AND THIS IS THE MEASUREMENT THAT SHOWS IT. The same model, the same prompt and the same temperature return the file complete once there is room for it. It also proves by measurement rather than by symptom that mac-16's refusal of this request was CORRECT: it needed 20,870 tokens in a 16,384-token window. What it does NOT settle is the mechanism -- why a response that ran out of room came back with a properly closed block and a run of 81 lines missing from the middle rather than cut off at the end. Nothing overflowed at 32,768, so this run cannot discriminate between the overflow policies

method: src/tools/repair.ts at 43,594 B. Estimated: input 43,594/3.9 + 200 = 11,378, output 43,594/3.5 = 12,455, total 23,833. Actual: 10,549 + 10,321 = 20,870. The estimator over-predicts the total by 14.2%, the input side by 7.9% and the output side by 20.7%. Measured output density on this file is 4.22 B per token against the 3.978 pooled over run 2026-08-04-mac-12-variance
note: OVER-PREDICTION IS THE SAFE DIRECTION AND THE MARGIN IS DOING WORK. At the real 16,384 window the estimate of 23,833 refused this request and the true need of 20,870 also exceeds it, so the refusal was right for the right reason rather than right by luck. Recorded next to B14's unapplied re-derivation: the output divisor stays at 3.5 against a measured 3.978 pooled and 4.22 here, and this run is why the pessimism is not obviously waste

method: The model was explicitly loaded at 32,768 and `lms ps` confirmed it before run 2026-08-04-mac-20-32k started. Some minutes later, with the server still answering 200 on /v1/models and no configuration touched, `lms ps` reported the same model loaded at 16,384 -- the default. A probe request whose prompt alone exceeded the window had failed with a dropped connection in between
note: THE CAUSE IS NOT ESTABLISHED AND IS NOT CLAIMED. Two workloads were competing for memory at the time: the oversized probe and a contract-stability run started concurrently, so the dropped connection cannot be attributed to either. The RELOAD is the fact, and it is enough: a declared window can go stale on its own, which is the exact state that admits a request the model cannot honour and returns a closed, well-formed, shorter file. Recorded under its own run id because it is an observation about the machine, not a result of any diagnostic

method: A second verified-window run was started to give B16 its required second non-void run. The pre-flight guard confirmed 32,768 at launch, but the loaded window fell to 16,384 while the run was in flight, and the oversized probe request was running against the same server at the same time. The artifact records loaded_context_length from a single probe at startup, so it would have claimed 32,768 for requests that may have been served at half that
note: DISCARDED RATHER THAN SCORED, AND DELETED RATHER THAN KEPT AS EVIDENCE. It reproduces exactly the defect that voids mac-19 -- a declared window the model did not have -- with the added problem that the discrepancy appeared MID-RUN, which a start-of-run probe cannot see. B16 still has one non-void run and needs a second. The operational lesson is separate and larger: a diagnostic must not share the machine with anything else, because memory pressure changes the thing being measured

method: Second non-void run, on a machine running nothing else. Window verified at 32,768 by `lms ps` BEFORE the run and again AFTER it, which is the check mac-21 lacked. 26 requests, 26 scored, 0 errored, 0 refused: complete 26, elided 0, truncated 0, probe applied in every file. Largest admitted request 20,870 actual tokens against a 29,491 usable budget, clearing the 70% non-void bar of 20,644
note: B16 HOLDS: 0 of 52 admitted requests across this run and 2026-08-04-mac-20-32k, against a hold condition of 0 over at least 20 across at least 2 non-void runs and a fall line of >10%. Every condition was pre-registered before either run. The post-run window check is new and is what separates this from mac-21, which was discarded for drifting mid-run

method: The two non-void runs use the same 13-case corpus, the same model and temperature 0.1. D8 had already measured 12 of 13 cases returning byte-identical output across repeats, and mac-23's L10 reproduces mac-20's exactly: prompt 10,549 + completion 10,321 = 20,870 in both
note: THE THRESHOLD TURNED OUT WEAKER THAN IT LOOKED, AND IT IS NOT BEING RAISED. 52 admitted requests is closer to n=1 replicated than to n=2 independent, because a near-deterministic sampler over one corpus reproduces itself. Tightening the condition after seeing it satisfied is the mirror image of loosening it after seeing it missed, so the verdict stands as pre-registered and this row is what stops 52 from being read as 52 independent observations. Two further limits: neither run REFUSED anything, so both confirm that admitted requests succeed and say nothing about whether the pre-flight refuses what it should; and it is one model at one window on one repository

method: Arithmetic over this repository, not a run: for each of the 15 src files that have a matching tests/*.test.ts, estimated need = bytes/3.9 + 200 + bytes/3.5, LF-normalized, against floor(window * 0.9). At a 16,384-token window 5 of 15 pairs exceed it (gate.ts, fs-safety.ts, selection.ts, contract-probe.ts, repair.ts); at 32,768 only 1 of 15 does (repair.ts + its test, 99,887 B). Files alone: 2 of 30 at 16,384, 0 of 30 at 32,768. Per-call ceiling ~26.8 KB at 16,384 and ~54.0 KB at 32,768
note: THE BASE RATE G7's PROTOCOL ASKS FOR, AND IT IS NOT A NUMBER BUT A FUNCTION OF THE WINDOW -- which is the finding. 33% against 7% for the same repository and the same estimator, differing only in what the model was loaded with, means a threshold on context_would_overflow is meaningless until the window is fixed. That is G7's rule 3 arriving from the other direction. NO THRESHOLD IS SET on it here: having the rate in hand is exactly when setting one is the move rule 4 exists to prevent. It also answers the practical question the operator asked -- a 16,384 window refuses a third of the natural work unit for repair and fix, which is a file plus its test

method: Direct read of ~/.lmstudio/.internal/http-server-config.json on the measuring machine: justInTimeModelLoading true, port 1234, verbose true, fileLoggingMode succinct, autoStartOnLaunch false. `lms --help` confirms the CLI has no configuration subcommand -- `lms get` downloads models and presets rather than reading local settings
note: THE NAMED CAUSE OF THE WINDOW DRIFT. JIT loading brings a model back when the server is asked for one that is not loaded, at the model's DEFAULT context rather than at whatever the last explicit `lms load` requested. It does not prove what happened on 2026-08-04 -- the crash still has two candidate causes -- but it removes the mystery: a window that was 32,768 by request and 16,384 afterwards is the documented behaviour of a setting that is on, and it needs no crash at all, since any unload is enough. Two consequences: LOCAL_CODER_CONTEXT_TOKENS is most dangerous exactly when JIT is on, because it is only consulted in the not-loaded state that JIT is about to contradict; and turning JIT off would make the failure loud, the server erroring instead of silently serving a differently-configured model

method: Searched ~/.lmstudio/.internal/ui-state, ~/.lmstudio/.internal/*.json and ~/.lmstudio/hub for contextOverflowPolicy, rollingWindow, truncateMiddle and stopAtLimit with binaries included: no match. `lms` exposes no configuration subcommand. The only earlier matches were the app's own bundled JavaScript and the @lmstudio/sdk type declarations
note: RETRACTS A STRONGER CLAIM MADE EARLIER. DECISIONS.md said the policy is in 'no user configuration file', which was overstated: that search used grep -I and skipped binary files, and it never looked in ~/Library/Application Support/, where an Electron app keeps its state on macOS. What is established is narrower -- not in the CLI, not in the data directory. The open point stays open, and it stays labelled a hypothesis

method: Six independent routes, all returning nothing: (1) `lms ps --json` reports contextLength and maxContextLength only; (2) `lms --help` shows no configuration subcommand, and `lms get` downloads models and presets rather than reading settings; (3) recursive search of ~/.lmstudio with binaries included, covering .internal/ui-state, .internal/*.json and hub; (4) ~/Library/Application Support holds nothing LM Studio related at all, confirmed by an unfiltered listing after a failed glob had silently aborted an earlier attempt; (5) `lms log stream` during a live request prints llm.prediction.input and llm.prediction.output and no prediction config; (6) the OpenAI-compatible endpoint rejects the field, per the open bug tracker issue 532
note: THE QUESTION 'CAN THIS BE READ PROGRAMMATICALLY' IS NOW ANSWERED SEPARATELY FROM 'WHAT IS ITS VALUE'. One route remains untried -- the @lmstudio/sdk, where contextOverflowPolicy is a declared type and which ships inside LM Studio's own plugin node_modules. The design consequence does not wait on it: a property this project can neither read nor set is one no shipped behaviour may depend on, which is why B16 counts the harm and names the mechanism only as an open question. That was decided before any of this was known, and it is why none of it blocks anything
